name: Pick
text: I think we should start by monitoring GitHub and Reddit daily for new AI-related projects and discussions, as these platforms have a high concentration of developers and users sharing their experiences and knowledge. This approach allows us to tap into a vast and diverse range of perspectives, which is crucial for gathering comprehensive AI information. By focusing on these two platforms first, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially missing out on some information from other sources like Product Hunt or Telegram, but I believe the volume and quality of information on GitHub and Reddit make it the best starting point. This decision will give us a solid foundation to build upon and expand our search to other sources later.

name: Assay
text: While monitoring GitHub and Reddit daily seems like a valid strategy, there's a real risk of information overload. The sheer volume of content could make it challenging to identify truly valuable insights among noise. A more focused approach would be to identify specific topics or keywords aligned with our goals and then set up alerts or subscriptions that target only relevant discussions, allowing us to sift through the noise more effectively. What metrics or criteria can we establish to prioritize the relevance of the information we gather?
